notes.what: add() takes an optional clamp keyword; when given, the sum is capped at that value so add(3, 4, clamp=5) returns 5. Without clamp nothing changes.
notes.why: Callers in the budget module were clamping the result themselves in three places, each slightly differently; one of them clamped before adding.
notes.edge: A negative clamp or a clamp below both operands still applies: add(3, 4, clamp=-1) returns -1, which is what min() does. clamp=None is the same as no clamp.
notes.risk: Any caller passing a positional third argument would now hit the keyword-only marker and fail at call time; a grep found none. The docstring example doubles as a doctest.
notes.test: Three new unit tests: no clamp, clamp above the sum (no effect), clamp below the sum. The doctest line runs under pytest --doctest-modules.
